moments.title: A worked NAV problem: equity 850, debt 50, cash 20, liability 15, 40 units
moments.summary: The facilitator reads out a fund statement and asks the room to calculate the NAV from it.
moments.evidence: Ganga blue chip fund statement, it shows that equity is 850 rupees, debt is 50 rupees, cash is 20 rupees, liability is 15 and the units outstanding are 40.

moments.title: "Debt" on a fund statement means the fund's debt investments
moments.summary: A clarification during the exercise: the debt line is not borrowing, it is the fund's debt investments, held alongside its equity investments.
moments.evidence: When we are referring to debt, it refers to debt investment.

moments.title: The NAV formula recalled: total assets minus liabilities, divided by units outstanding
moments.summary: When the room stalls, the facilitator gives the hint that unlocks it — the formula itself.
moments.evidence: Remember, the formula to calculate the NAV was total assets minus liabilities divided by units outstanding.
